# Saradom — LLM build reference

Architecture pattern (not a framework/library): plain HTML + JS, no build, no bundler, no imports.
This file is a working cheat-sheet for an agent building modules/components in this repo.

## 1. Foundations

- State lives in the DOM (attribute, input `value`, `textContent`, `data-*`, or `_`-prefixed JS prop for handles like `el._timer`) — never in JS variables. The DOM is the single source of truth; no reactivity runtime, no sync.
- Events are set inline in HTML attributes (`onclick="Todo.Add(this)"`) — never `addEventListener`; markup inserted later is live at once, nothing to unbind.
- Module name = prefix of its attributes: object `Accordion` owns `accordion-*` markup; CSS targets the same attributes (`[todo-item-status="done"]`). Module is an IIFE returning its public API; all modules hang off one global `App`, folder-like dotted names.
- UI is interactive as it parses (state comes ready from backend); components needing setup init in place, never via `DOMContentLoaded`/`defer`.
- Interaction = direct DOM write on the element the handler already holds — no diff, no scheduler.

## 2. Building a module (algorithm)

1. **Structure** — lay out the elements the module needs.
2. **Events** — define where an action *starts* (click, drag, input, submit…) as an inline attribute handler.
3. **Prefixed attribute markers** — tag elements with `module-*` attributes the JS reads/writes. This is the **explicit contract** between HTML and JS (no type system).

**Tool priority** (stop at the first that fits): native HTML → htmx (`Hx`) → generic toolkits (`Notify`/`Switch`/`Filter`/`Compute`/`Sortable`/`Util`) → your own small component last.

## 3. Signature notation

A signature is the contract: namespaced attributes, their values, the functions run on them, and nesting (`<` = element, indentation = descendant). Functions that touch storage/other elements listed below.

```
< pin-space pin-store="detail-properties">
    < pin-target>                                  # where pinned items move to
    < pin-name="propA" pin-on?>                     # instance root; pin-on flag when pinned
        < pin-slot="propA">                         # original home, for restore
        < onclick="Pin.Toggle(this)">
    < script>Pin.Init(document.currentScript)</script>   # OR: <s-init run="(el)=>el.restore()">

Pin.Toggle(btn)  Pin.Init(script)   # store = ordered array of pinned names in localStorage[pin-store]
```

## 4. Gotchas (bad → good)

- **State in a CSS class → bad.** `classList.toggle('nav-off')` + CSS `.app.nav-off{…}` is wrong on both sides: state must live in an **attribute** and CSS must target that attribute. Use `el.flag('nav-off', !el.flag('nav-off'))` (Util: no 2nd arg = read, `true/false` = set/remove) and style `[nav-off]{…}` / `.app[nav-off] .sidebar{…}`. Classes are for **styling only** — never for state, never as a JS/CSS contract. Same for values: `attr('field-state','done')` + `[field-state="done"]`, not a `.is-done` class.
- Grabbing by class / `parentElement` / siblings in JS → **bad**. Only by **prefixed attributes** (`.one/.all/.up` from Util). HTML may be rearranged; the attribute is the contract.
- Module built for one specific thing → **bad**. Modules are **generic**; the value comes from the DOM (attribute or `textContent`), marked by the contract.
- `document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded')` or `defer` for init → **bad** (too late, breaks UX-Performance). Init **in place**: inline `Component.Init(document.currentScript)`, or `<s-init run="(el)=>el.restore()">` as the **last child** (a custom element that reads children upgrades in `connectedCallback` *before* its children are parsed — so `s-init` goes last, after the children it acts on).
- Store key on a sub-element → **bad**; it belongs on the instance **root**. One store, not two (membership + order = a single ordered array of names).
- Coupling: an element carries **two attributes with the same value** (`pin-name` + `sort-item`); each module reads **only its own**. They "communicate" via equal value + shared storage key, never by reading each other's attributes.
- Module prefix = the module's **own full name**, unique — never a short/generic truncation. `InlineEdit` owns `inline-edit-*`, **not** `inline-*` (leave `inline-*` free so a future `Inline` module can't collide). The prefix reserves a namespace; a generic stem is a landmine.
- View↔edit toggle (inline editing) → **don't write a JS component**; each editable thing gets its OWN pair of partials named for what it is (`title-show.html` ↔ `title-edit.html`, `field-show` ↔ `field-edit`), each hard-referencing the other — no generic input partial, no `back` parameter. Click show → POST the edit partial pre-filled; Enter/blur → POST the show partial with the value (`hx-fill` substitutes). Reach for a JS module only when HX genuinely can't express it.
- `id` only for native `popover`/`<dialog>`; otherwise a generic `[dropdown]` (trigger+menu bound by structure), not an id per menu.
- htmx does **not** show the dropdown — the native `popover` does; htmx only loads content: `dropdown-onopen="hx(this)"`. `hx(this)` **without `event`** = no `preventDefault`, so the native action (popover) still fires; `hx(this,event)` in a form = `preventDefault`.
- Auto-popover light-dismiss + open-on-`focus` → **bad** (the click that gives focus opens the popover, the same click's `click` phase light-dismisses it). Use `popover="manual"` and close yourself with inline routers on `body` (like `Shortcut.Route`, never `addEventListener`): `Dropdown.Down` on `onpointerdown` (click outside the space → close), `Dropdown.Out` on `onfocusout` (Tab to a CONCRETE element outside → close; ignore `relatedTarget=null` — lost focus is an artifact of e.g. SortableJS moving the focused element mid-drag, not a user action), `Dropdown.Esc` on `onkeydown`. Closing on focusout alone breaks drag-inside-menu and misses outside clicks when focus sits on `body`.
- Our `Hx`: `hx-target` supports `closest <sel>` (+ descendant after it), but **not** `find` after `closest`; `hx-swap` = `innerHTML|outerHTML|append|prepend|none` (**not** `beforeend`).
- Name the storage key by **what it is** and whether it's a global preference or instance state (`detail-properties`, not `scrum1`).
- Util helpers (`.one/.all/.up/.attr/.flag/.run`) live on `HTMLElement.prototype` — they throw on **SVG** elements (`<use>`, `<svg>`). For SVG use native `get/setAttribute`.

## 5. Toolkits — quick contract

- **`Hx`** — `hx-get|post|put|delete|patch="url"`, `hx-target` (`this` | `closest <sel> [desc]` | selector), `hx-swap` (`innerHTML`(default)`|outerHTML|append|prepend|none`), `hx-select`, `hx-indicator`, `hx-disable`. Trigger `hx(this[,event])`; form/anchor bodies auto-built. Owner resolved via `closest([hx-*])`.
- **`Notify`** — `el.nup(name,data,stop?)` / `el.ndown(...)` / `el.nall(name,data)`; listener = an attribute `name="(data)=>…"` eval'd with `this`=element. Up walks ancestors, Down walks descendants, All = whole document.
- **`Switch`** — tagged targets flipped by tag set; the space is ANY selector passed in the call. `Switch.To(ctx, '[switch-space]', 'a b')` turns on every `[switch-tag]` whose tag is in the set, off the rest, mirrors to `switch-state`; `Switch.Toggle(ctx, space, when, then, otherwise)`. `switch-config-tag` on the space renames the tag attribute; `switch-onchange="(on)=>…"` on a target replaces show/hide with any effect. (Supersedes the old `Visible`.)
- **`Filter`** — `[filter-space]` (opt `filter-lane`), `[filter-query]` input `oninput="Filter.Filter(this)"`, `[filter-item="searchable text"]` rows toggled by substring.
- **`Dropdown`** (`Dropdown/Dropdown.js` + `Dropdown.css`) — `[dropdown-space dropdown-onopen? dropdown-onclose?]` wraps `[dropdown-trigger onclick="Dropdown.Toggle(this)"]` (or `onfocus="Dropdown.Open(this)"`) + `[dropdown-menu popover="manual"]`. The onopen/onclose hooks live on the SPACE (component root, `this`=space — find the menu via `this.one('[dropdown-menu]')`), never on the menu. CSS anchors per instance (`anchor-scope:--dd` on the space — N dropdowns don't collide, no ids). Closing via three inline routers on `body`: `onpointerdown="Dropdown.Down(event)"`, `onfocusout="Dropdown.Out(event)"`, `onkeydown="…; Dropdown.Esc(event)"`. `dropdown-pin` flag on the menu = routers skip it, closes only via `Dropdown.Close(ctx)` or the trigger's Toggle. Menu position = the VALUE of `dropdown-menu`: empty (default, under the trigger) | `bottom-end` | `top` | `top-end` | `right` | `left` — a preference, not a promise: `position-try-fallbacks` in the toolkit CSS flips the panel when there is no room (footer dropdown becomes a drop-up by itself). Chrome/Edge only (CSS anchor positioning).
- **`Util`** (globals, no import) — `el.one/all(sel)`, `el.up(sel)` (self-or-closest, falls back to body), `el.attr(a[,v])`, `el.attrt(a,v1,v2)` (toggle), `el.flag(f[,bool])`, `el.run(attr)` (eval attr, call if fn), `el.hide/show/clear`, `document.one/al(sel)`, `Array#each/any/none`, `String#cut(n)`. `dom` = `document`.
- **`<s-sortable>`** (SortableJS wrapper) — attrs `group`,`boundary`(put-guard sel),`handle`,`animation`,`onsort`. `store="key"` + `[sort-item="name"]` persist order to localStorage; call `restore()` (via a trailing `<s-init run="(el)=>el.restore()">`) to reapply.
- **`<s-compute run="() => …">`** — MutationObserver on children (add `shallow` for childList-only, `debounce="ms"`, `guard`); recomputes derived DOM (counts, bars) on any change. `this`=the element.
- **`<s-init run="(el)=>…">`** — runs once in `connectedCallback` with `this`=parent; the in-place init primitive.
- **`<s-resizer store var min max>`** inside `[resizer-space]` — drag to set a CSS var (default `--panel-w`) on the space, clamped `min`..`max`, persisted to `localStorage[store]`. Attribute naming rule for custom elements: BARE names on the element's own tag (the tag is the namespace: `run`, `handle`, `store`, `min`), module-prefixed names on foreign elements (`sort-item` on list children, `resizer-space` on the wrapper).
- **`Modal`** (global; `include_once` `Modal.html` = `<style>` + `<template modal-tpl>` + `<script>` once) — `Modal.Open(url, callback)` loads an app page (GET) in a fullscreen dialog; the page adds `_modal=1` to drop its layout. The page inside calls `Modal.Result(data)` / `Modal.Cancel()` (and routes Escape with `<body onkeydown="Modal.Esc(event)">`), forwarded through `window.parent`; callback runs with the value or `null`. Anti-flicker: dialog opens on `iframe.onload` (instant) or after 500ms (`modal-state="loading"`→`"iframe"`). Picker: `_pick=1` + choose-posts-to-self, controller returns via `Modal.Result`.
